questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to do my exchange within europe and I have not been to Italy before. And also I looked at courses from different University around Europe and the courses at University of Milan aligned best with what I wanted.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The personal experience was perfect, but there was some problems with the University and stuff like that.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Kind of hard, there wasnt really a lot of help to get and you had to figure it out yourself.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did get a couple of mails with information, but it was always last minute and still needed to figure out stuff myself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Massimo, the coordinator at the university of Milan, was good at answering emails when I had question

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Be out in good time, I ended living in a quite expensive airbnb.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think it is more fun socially to live at some of the dorms through the university. I had a lot of friends who lived at campus Martinitt, and I kinda wished that I had lived there myself (its also quite cheap).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was really last minute you registrered for the courses and I ended missing my first lecture because I didnt get the schedule in time.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You found your courses and registrered thtough a website, the university sent an email with a guide how to. It took some to get the registration approved

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could contact the international office at the university

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended getting all the courses i wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You have to figure your schedule out yourself (with overlapping classes etc.), so look at it in good time

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I do not think the academic level was high and the teaching wasnt that good. They also have a really different exam system, so I would recommend looking for courses with written exams.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I could not feel that i was taking master courses, I would say the level of the courses is like the level of bachelors courses at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was only verbal lectures, where the teachers just talked for 1,5-2 hours. I didnt like the teaching and skipped quite many classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Genetics, cellular and molecular biology
Ecology
Methods in bioinformatics
Molecular and cellular microbiology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Ecology was a really good and interesting course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I dont think I had any unexpected costs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee was really cheap, which was really nice. Going out to eat is also in general cheaper than Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think they could have a better intro in the start of the semester and do more to make sure the exchange student get on socially. I ended finding a big friend group, but that was not through the university or the student clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is ESN, which is a student erasmus club, that hosts different social events, trips etc. for erasmus students

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to many of the ESN events in the start of the semester and meet new people throgh that, also go to Milan 1-2 weeks before the academic semester starts.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went to a lot of different city in italy during my weekends (Rome, Bologna, Como, Venice) also a lot og hike trips to the mountains (both Italy and Switzerland). I also went on a trip to morocco for 6 days, really fun trip

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think the Italians in general is just less effective that danes, and that was really hard to adjust to

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to the italians in your classes

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language sometimes, as quite many Italians dont speak english

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go to Milan 1-2 weeks before the semester starts, so you can go to the different events there is and meet people. Live at one of the dorms, make its easier to socialize and expect a really hard exam period (I had 4 exams in 1,5 weeks).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No not really

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I have really learned a lot about myself and I hav met so many different people and got tons of new friends from all over europe.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The exam periode was really hard

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
